correctness.rationale: For any strictly positive fitness, the 16-state Markov chain is absorbing and its exact hitting vector solves (I-Q)f=r. Symmetry-lumped 10- and 5-state exact eliminations give the stated two-parameter rational identity and one-parameter rational formulas. Their numerator/denominator identities were symbolically checked. All coefficients of the general denominator are positive on the required nonnegative cone; the cost-specific transformed denominator and gap numerator have strictly positive coefficients. The threshold numerator after c=2t/(1+t) has one sign change, a negative constant and positive leading coefficient, proving precisely one positive root and hence one root in (0,2). Independent unquotiented 14-state exact inversions match across several parameters. No finite calculation is used as a substitute for a general argument.

value.rationale: The edge-color C4 model isolates a mathematically motivated question of whether an unchanged two-high/two-low payoff multiset and fixed degree sequence suffice to predict selection. The answer is an all-strength exact neutral-versus-superneutral dichotomy, not a tiny numerical gain or table lookup; a positive-cost theorem additionally gives an exact, unique cost boundary with opposite qualitative fixation decisions and demonstrates strict layout dominance across the full physically admissible interval. It is a targeted finite structural theorem with intrinsic value as an analytically solvable benchmark for quenched interaction heterogeneity, without asserting unproven generalization to larger networks.
